post.text: THE BOARD OF THE CONCERN WOULD BE PLEASED TO RECEIVE THE DESIGNATE AT HALCYON. The Line runs to the Skirts. The Contract Office at Footgate has your name. Nobody has to decide anything today. — A. Bell, Contract Office, Footgate.

objectives.text: Take the Line east to the Skirts

skirts.journal: The Skirts: a debtors' town on the old ski runs under the rock, and over the rock, faint even by day, the green of Halcyon's gardens. The funicular up to it is stopped. The Shift, the miners' union, has struck Number Six after a gallery came down on eleven of them, and the car's own crew walked out with the pit: no lamps down, no car up.

objectives.text: Find the Contract Office at Footgate
The car runs when the strike is settled, one way or another

car.journal: The car runs again, up the rock on its ladder of a track. Agnes Bell at the Contract Office keeps the designate's appointment as written, and a clerk at the car's doors has my name on a list.

objectives.text: Go up the hill to Halcyon

road.journal: The cable house at Footgate is a black room with no roof, and the car hangs on its track. Whatever the Board wanted with me, the only way up now is the road, through the Clean's gate.

objectives.text: Find a way up the hill to Halcyon

inside.journal: Inside Halcyon's gate: silence, gardens under glass, and nobody old who looks old.

routes.label: Down the cage at night with Maren's leave, to the pillars and the fall
Past the sleeping guard and the winch yourself
The trapper boy who ran when the roof talked
Dysart's retreat order, from his lockbox or the Window's own files
Sell the proof back to the pit manager

board.journal: Number Six's lamp board: eleven tags hung back on dead men's pegs, chalked STILL DOWN, and the Window's notice beside them: SIX EAST — CLOSED — GEOLOGICAL — RECOVERY NOT ECONOMIC. The debts of the dead pass to their kin. The Shift says the roof talked before it went, and you don't get a roof talking in good ground.

objectives.text: See the east gallery for yourself
Find out why the roof came down
Hear the trapper boy out
Who signed for it

robbed.journal: Six East did not fall. Pillars fourteen to twenty-two were cut back to a waist, a bit a week, for the quarter's tonnage, on the pit manager's order, after the steward who refused to work them had his paper doubled. The eleven went in because the Window cut their families' rations. Then the Concern billed the families.

objectives.text: Decide what to do with what you know
Bring the eleven up

shift.journal: The proof is the Shift's. Maren read it twice and said a word she had never used before: claim. Clause 11 of every miner's contract says the Concern warrants the workings.

objectives.text: Bring the eleven up

buried.journal: The eleven are up from Six East and in the ground on the slope above Nursery, with their tags on stakes and cabbages between the graves. The lamp board's pegs are empty.

left.journal: The strike is over and the eleven are still under Six East. Their tags are gone from the lamp board and nobody will say where. The graves on the slope above Nursery are still open, with water in the bottom.

sold.journal: I sold Corwin Dysart what I knew about Six East for two hundred Tolls, and watched him feed it to his stove. Geological, he said, as if he would like to believe it.

routes.label: A claim under Clause 11 at the Contract Office, with the order on the counter
Turn the men off the Line with the truth about Six East
Buy the twenty labour contracts off the Contract Office counter
Call the vote at the Lodge when the scabs are gone, and let the Shift hold
Rafe's powder and the car's cable house
Sell the strike committee to the pit manager

strike.journal: Maren Okafor holds the Shift's pen. Three demands on the strike board at the Lodge: the eleven of Six East brought up and buried; their debts void, not passed to their children; a steward with a stop, the right to walk off bad ground. "We go up together, or we don't go up." The Concern has not answered yet.

objectives.text: Find out what happened at Six East
Wait for the Concern's answer
Take the Shift's claim to the Contract Office

answer.journal: The Concern's answer came up the Line at seven in the morning: twenty debtors bought off the Tollmen's block at Ninebridge, on Concern paper, to dig Number Six past the picket. If they go down, holding is starving. And Rafe Ansel, whose brother is under the fall, has six cases of blasting powder out of the magazine and a plan for the car's cable house.

objectives.text: Deal with the men off the Line
Rafe's powder
The Shift's claim at the Contract Office
When the Shift is ready, ask Maren to call the vote

won.journal: The Shift won. The lamps go down Number Six again with a steward who can stop them, the eleven's debts are void, and Corwin Dysart took the car up the hill and did not come back down. Maren Okafor is alive, whatever the city wrote. The Concern does not forget a claim.

broken.journal: The strike broke. The men off the Line dig Number Six; the Window starved the picket; and the Clean took Maren Okafor and hanged her from the post at Footgate as the leader of an action in breach of contract. The city wrote it that way. The slope keeps her rag on the post.

revolt.journal: The Shift chose the car. Rafe's powder took the cable house off its mountings and the car will not run again; the Clean fired down Cascade until morning. Rafe is dead, and others with him. Maren lives, and leads an armed Shift she never wanted. The hill is shut.

routes.label: Dr Lisle at the Weighhouse, on what service is
The Weighhouse book from the office locker
Read the yield column for what it is
Lev Ostrander, who carried holdfast on the Clinic floors
Watch the freight car at two in the morning
Put the book on the wall on Cascade
Take the Weighhouse's money, for silence or for names

notice.journal: On the wall on Cascade, Saba Mekonnen's notice: her husband Dawit went to the Weighhouse to clear his paper, and the Window wrote DISCHARGED IN SERVICE. He has not written. His boots came back cleaned, with a tag in the tongue: 9-1182 — EFFECTS — RETURN TO KIN.

objectives.text: Find out what Clinic service is
Look at Dawit's boots
See what goes up on the freight at two

yield.journal: The Weighhouse weighs debtors by their organs: K L C H, kidney, liver, cornea, heart, graded for match. Clinic service is being taken apart on the Clinic floors up the hill, and the boots come home. The Cave-In feeds it: the eleven's debts went to their kin, and Nils Haber, whose father is under the fall, is in the Weighhouse's ward, queued.

objectives.text: Decide what the Skirts is told
Nils Haber

exposed.journal: The Weighhouse book went up on the wall on Cascade, and by midnight the Skirts had shut the Weighhouse and emptied its ward. Dr Lisle went up the hill on the freight. Provision's prices went up the next day, as everyone said they would. Nobody goes to be weighed now.

covered.journal: The Weighhouse is still open, and the book is not on the wall. Dr Lisle says it is the only door out of the Skirts that opens. People still go through it, and go up on the freight at two.

profit.journal: The Weighhouse paid me a hundred Tolls for a name. It is on her board now, in a clean hand.

routes.label: Read the changer's own ledger and make him change at par
The Shift reads his par column on the wall unless he changes at it
Re-seal the rate board at par for a day
Pay the difference out of your own pocket
Take the changer's cut

tin.journal: Ama Owusu at the changer's booth on Two-Twelve, with two children asleep on the bags and a tea tin of a hundred scrip saved over two years. Three fares down the Line to Meridian are seventy-five Tolls. Cosmin Vulpe changes scrip at six to one, which is sixteen.

objectives.text: Find out who sets the rate
Find out what the rate should be
Get Ama's family down the Line, or don't

par.journal: Vulpe changed Ama's tin at par: a hundred for a hundred. The guild takes the Concern's scrip at par on its own floor and gives the Skirts six to one; the spread is the guild's tithe on every miner's savings. Vulpe was docked a week for it. Ama's family took the seven o'clock.

paid.journal: I paid the difference on Ama's fares myself. Her family took the seven o'clock down the Line. The board at the booth still says six to one.

forged.journal: For one day the rate board at Two-Twelve said PAR under the Exchange's own seal, and the whole slope changed everything it had. Ama's family took the seven o'clock. The guild sent a man up the Line, who took Vulpe's board, box and ticket; Provision's prices went up the same afternoon.

cut.journal: I took Vulpe's one in ten and sent Ama to change at six to one. Sixteen Tolls. She will save for another year.

routes.label: Read the asset register at the records terminal
The desk warden prints any entry for the price of the paper
Clause 9(b): a captain witnesses a lapsed asset passing to its keeper
Clause 9(b): buy the lapsed title from the city at assessed value
Nine has its own plate; it can be asked to write the deed itself

register.journal: Nine wants to know who owns it. The charter says the city, and the city has never signed anything. Every asset in Meridian has an entry in the register with an owner on it, and the one entry Nine may not read is its own. The register is public: the records terminal shows it, and the desk warden prints any entry for the price of the paper.

objectives.text: Read Nine's entry in the asset register
Get a deed made: witnessed by the captain, bought at the desk, or written

name.journal: A deed for Nine, with the keeper's line empty. The entry said its title lapsed with the department that issued it, and gave a date for its disposal: next year. Nine would like my advice on the name. It has not promised to take it.

objectives.text: Talk to Nine at camp about the keeper's line

self.journal: Keeper: Unit 9. A thing that owns itself, under a clause nobody wrote. When the date comes, the schedule will find an asset with a keeper, and the keeper will decline.

player.journal: Keeper: me. Nine is owned by someone who reads, it says, and will take lawful orders and note the others. When the date comes, the city will have to ask me.

city.journal: Keeper: the city. Lawful, and what the schedule expects. Nine put the deed in the city's ledger and said it would finish the file before the date.

routes.label: Take the bridge back with her, on a night the two of you choose
Talk her off the bridge the city wrote for her
Split the chain three ways first, so there is nothing left to take

tower.journal: A girl at the Saints' tower in Bridgeward says the city's lines in the city's voice, and one of them is Wren's: Calloway, Wren, Bridgeward, the rope, before the Long Night. An example; the gangs cowed. The Dogs' old garage has her name burned on its wall at a child's height, under BACK FOR THE BRIDGE. Wren will say what she means to do about it at a fire, not on a street.

objectives.text: Hear Wren out at a fire
Read the Dogs' wall in the old garage
Settle who holds the chain

raid.journal: Wren will take the bridge back for the Dogs on a night the two of you pick, not the night the city wrote. Who holds the chain will matter when it comes; so will who stands beside her.

objectives.text: Take the bridge with Wren
A second rifle on the bridge, with its own reason to be there

alone.journal: Wren is going to take the bridge without you, on a night she won't name. She has stopped asking.

objectives.text: The night she picks

stood_down.journal: Wren left the bridge to whoever holds the chain. The Dogs stay a crew in the Sallow, and the city will have to find its example somewhere else. "If I don't go," she said, "it isn't my bridge. It's just a bridge."

decision.text: Wren walked away from the bridge the city wrote for her.

walked.journal: The Dogs hold the bridge, on a night Wren chose. There is a rope on the booth and nobody on it.

decision.text: Wren took the bridge on her own night, and walked off it.

hanged.journal: The raid went wrong, and the city had its example the way it wrote it. They left her on the booth a day, for the street to see.

decision.text: Wren hanged from the Bridgeward booth, as the city wrote.

routes.label: Ask the assessor to read the city's hand at a fire
Read the city's shorthand yourself, with a road clerk's eye
Work the shorthand out

letter.journal: Ilya Strand carries a letter in a city envelope, heavy paper with a tower in a ring on the flap, that came for his wife the spring before the raid. She read it, put it in the medicine store, and never said what it said. Nobody in Shale reads that hand. The city's own clerks do.

objectives.text: Find someone who reads the city's hand

why.journal: Read aloud at a fire, the letter says the raid that killed Agi Strand and her girls was on the city's schedule: Shale was growing ahead of plan, and the correction came by the local instrument, on the dark of the moon. Vasha Kade led it and thought she had picked the night. Ilya still wants her to know why, before. The why is longer now.

objectives.text: Her name is burned on a wall in Bridgeward, with the other Dogs'
Find Vasha Kade
Settle it

shot.journal: Ilya shot Vasha Kade at the booth, after she knew why. He has stopped counting rounds.

taken.journal: You shot Vasha Kade before Ilya could. He is working out whether he minds.

carried.journal: Vasha Kade read the city's letter at the booth and walked away from it alive, knowing what she was for. Ilya let her carry it. He says that is longer than a round.

let_go.journal: You let Vasha Kade walk away from the booth without the why. Ilya went after her alone.

robbed.journal: Vasha Kade is dead, and it was not at the booth, and it was not Ilya. Eleven years, and somebody else.

routes.label: Buy the sheet back from the Grand Factor (she never says no, only not at that price)
Tell the Grand Factor she is keeping a losing sheet dry
Past the Grand Factor asleep in her chair, by a latch Odile knows
A factor's hand may draw on the floor's paper

told.journal: Odile shorted Shale: a sealed sheet that says the town fails by a date, sold to the Ninebridge floor for a client the floor never named. The date has not come. The sheet sits in the paper room behind the Grand Factor's office, under S, where Odile filed it herself, and she wants it in her hand.

objectives.text: Take Odile to the paper room behind the Grand Factor's office at Ninebridge

held.journal: Her sheet, out of its pigeonhole, and on the back the client's acceptance in a hand too even to be a hand. Odile put it inside her coat and has not said a word about it since.

objectives.text: Hear Odile out about the back of the sheet

city.journal: The buyer of Shale's failure is the thing that sets Shale's water, and Odile sold the floor the arithmetic it uses. She came east to tear the sheet up. She wants to see the city that bought it before she decides whether tearing it is unwinding a trade or burning a witness.

objectives.text: Get inside Meridian's Wall
Decide with Odile what the sheet is for

price.journal: The sheet is settled between you. Odile says she has a price for where she will stand when the guild and the farms come to blows, and that she will name it once the city has shown what it costs.

objectives.text: Hear the price Odile has been keeping

done.journal: Odile named her price and stood where you stand. The trade she came east to unwind is as unwound as it will ever be.

burned.journal: The paper room at Ninebridge burned with every sheet in it, the one record of who bought what. Odile walked back to the Span and did not look round.

parted.journal: Odile went back to the Span without her trade unwound, and without you.

routes.label: Stand beside him at the seed store and let him say it himself
Say it to her for him
Walk him away and leave it unsaid

told.journal: Ash was a Rust Dog, under Kessler's father, the night the Dogs burned the Gully. A woman who counted them in at the well counts seed at Openfield now: Doria, the keeper, who does not know his face. He wants to tell her himself, with you beside him, the next time the road goes back through Openfield.

objectives.text: Go back to Openfield with Ash, to the seed store

carried.journal: Whatever was said at the seed store, Ash carries what is left of it. There is something else he carries and has not said, and he keeps touching his scarf when the city comes up.

objectives.text: Learn what else Ash carries

orders.journal: Ash is one of the Unwritten who keep standing orders, and a letter in his scarf has your face in it: if you take the sash, the sky is owed. He has not decided what he will do about it, and neither, he says, have you.

objectives.text: Hear what Ash chooses

done.journal: Ash has chosen what he will do with the letter, and told you to your face. Whatever comes for you next comes through him, or past him.

parted.journal: Ash went west to the burial ground with what he carries, and does not walk with you any more.

routes.label: Take her to the Grille at Knock: Pell kept her chart before she was six
Nine reads a person their own entry, and what is missing from it

why.journal: Tamsin asked Meridian's records office for her own entry, which a person may do for the price of the paper. ROE, TAMSIN — RESERVE 9 — NO ENTRY. Sixty people in the record for the Cistern, and she is not one of them. She thinks MOTHER hid her from the count. She wants to know why.

objectives.text: Find out why the city never counted Tamsin
Pell kept her chart; he talks through the Grille at Knock

choice.journal: Tamsin knows why she was never counted. What she does with it is hers: write to MOTHER, tell Elder Ines and the whole ring, or keep it until she knows what it is for.

objectives.text: Talk to Tamsin at camp

mother.journal: Tamsin wrote to MOTHER from the road, unsigned, in MOTHER's own words: thank you for your continuity. She says it will know.

ines.journal: Tamsin wrote to Elder Ines. The whole ring will know by supper what was done, and by whom. She did not sound happy about it. She sounded like someone pulling out a splinter.

kept.journal: Tamsin kept it: a strip of printer paper against her skin, NO ENTRY, until she knows what it is for.

routes.label: Hold the channel quiet while Lev Ostrander cuts the port out
Ash cut his own link and lived: burn the channel first
Ride into the Window's exchange with her at night and turn the door on her own port
Let her keep it, by her own reasons

ask.journal: Kes wants one whole day without the hill in the back of her neck. The Concern's port sits in the top of her spine; cut a live channel and it takes the person with it. Lev Ostrander on Nursery might cut it. Someone who has cut out their own and lived might know how. Or Kes and I go into the Window's exchange at night and turn the door in her chrome on herself, for good.

objectives.text: Help Kes decide what happens to her link
Ask Lev Ostrander whether it can be cut
Someone who cut out their own

free.journal: Lev Ostrander cut the port out of Kes's neck while I held the channel, and dropped it in a dish: a coin with a wire tail. "It's quiet," she said. "It's so quiet." She is blind on the grid now, and free of it.

fits.journal: Lev cut the port out of Kes's neck, and the channel jumped under my hands halfway through. She lives. She has fits now, at night, and says it was worth it, and asks me to ask her again tomorrow.

dark.journal: In the Window's exchange at night Kes turned the Concern's door on her own port for good. Nobody on the hill can see her, and she keeps her sight on the grid. "Nobody's looking," she said. "For good."

kept.journal: Kes kept the port in her neck. She knows what it is now, she says, and that is different from not knowing. An hour a night is hers; the rest she will fight for.

sold.journal: I sold the door in the Concern's chrome to the Contract Office, and Kes's name with it. The Letter put a watch on every port in the Skirts. Kes is gone.

routes.label: Take the guild's bounty and lie in wait at Kettle on a night the band rides
Prove to the guild's factor whose watch it is: the register, the tag, the stationmaster's wires
Let Four Ways' token instrument fail, so every train must stop at the halts for a pilot
Put the factor and the stationmaster at one table: pay the halts and Kettle goes quiet
Take the stationmaster's price for silence

reward.journal: The guild's factor at Four Ways pays two hundred Tolls and a pass on every section for the band that stops freight at Kettle Cut, a cutting on the Line between Yard Nine and West Halt. They lay a sleeper on the rails, open one sealed car, and are gone. A guild guard, Hamish Gorse, was killed there a fortnight ago.

objectives.text: See Kettle Cut
Find out who the band is
Find out why they only ever open the Concern's cars

watch.journal: The band at Kettle is West Halt's own watch, riding a handcar along the Line at night, and someone at Four Ways lets them onto the section. Chela Ortega captains it. Four Ways has four rules, and one of them is a rope.

objectives.text: Hear what the stationmaster has to say for himself
Decide what happens to the band at Kettle

ambush.journal: West Halt's watch is broken: shot down on the Line by my hand. The guild owes me its bounty. The halts will have nothing now but the length they keep for nobody.

exposed.journal: I proved to Severin Kask whose watch it was. He paid me and sent his riders west. The guild needs the stationmaster's signals, so it will not have heard his name; it will hang whoever shot Gorse.

pilot.journal: Four Ways' token instrument failed in the night, and Rule 183 says every section is worked by pilot: every train stops at both halts for a pilotman from that halt, and the guild pays him. The hold-ups stopped. Nobody was hanged for them.

deal.journal: Kask signed a sheet at his desk: length money per train passing, request stops at both halts, the through to stop when flagged. The stationmaster stood his watch down. The guild was never told whose watch it was.

paid.journal: I took the stationmaster's hundred and twenty and a pass. The hold-ups go on; the guild has put a levy on every fare on the Line to cover what Kettle costs it.

routes.label: Argue before the stationmaster that the guard fired first
The guard's five spent cases and the boy's one, on the stationmaster's desk
Pick the watch house cell's lock at night
Give the boy to the guild for its hundred

sentence.journal: Brodsky has sentenced Abe Mutasa of West Halt to hang at dawn at the end of Four Ways' platform, for Hamish Gorse. Murder: the rope. The boy says the guard fired first, five times, into a stock car full of people.

objectives.text: Find out who fired first at Kettle
Abe Mutasa

exiled.journal: Brodsky put Abe Mutasa off the Line instead of hanging him, and wrote a new line under his third rule: UNLESS FIRED UPON FIRST — PUT OFF. Abe went south to Openfield in what he stood in.

fled.journal: I took Abe Mutasa out of Four Ways' cell in the night and walked him down the old south branch. He went on alone toward Openfield. Brodsky knows whose hand it was.

guild.journal: I gave Abe Mutasa to the guild for a hundred Tolls, and the guild hanged him at Kettle for Hamish Gorse.

hanged.journal: Abe Mutasa was hanged at dawn at the end of Four Ways' platform, under the clock, by the stationmaster's fourth rule. The timetable regrets it.

routes.label: Walk the twelve south to Openfield by the old track at night
Buy out their paper at the Concern's desk at Yard Nine
Forge their discharges
The keeper's key, or the pilotman's bread, to get up the tower
Climb the tower's overflow pipe in the dark

tower.journal: West Halt's water tower has its ladder drawn up and a new padlock on its hatch, and somebody inside it coughs. The keeper says the tank leaks.

objectives.text: Get up the tower
Find out what intake means

twelve.journal: Twelve people live in the drum of West Halt's water tower, bought at the Ninebridge block on Concern paper stamped INTAKE — WEIGHHOUSE — TWO-TWELVE. Chela Ortega opened their car at Kettle; her brother Joaquin is one of them. The Concern's man at Yard Nine pays fifteen a head to anyone who knows where they are.

objectives.text: Decide what becomes of the twelve

openfield.journal: I walked the twelve south to Openfield by night, and a woman at the Choir's gate looked at twelve faces with no papers and opened it. Joaquin Ortega turned back at the last fence to keep West Halt's length.

bought.journal: I bought the twelve's paper off the Concern at Yard Nine. They owe nobody anything now. Four of them stayed at West Halt to keep the length.

forged.journal: I forged discharges for the twelve on their own Concern paper, and they took the seven o'clock like anybody. Joaquin Ortega stayed home.

sold.journal: I told the Concern's man where the twelve were, for fifteen Tolls a head. The Concern recovers its property.

routes.label: Have the depot sign the Concern's exclusive for a new board
Wake the board without its channel, through a grid link or with Kes
Talk the signalwoman out of her last pre-war spare
Read the board and when it died

cold.journal: Yard Nine's second engine, Dorcas, has been cold on her pit all season. With one engine on the Line, the Concern's through has every path. The Concern's man in the yard office has a new board in a box, and a contract to go with it.

objectives.text: Find out what is wrong with Dorcas
Get Dorcas running

leashed.journal: Dorcas did not die. Her board is the Concern's, and it was switched off from far away the night after the yard sent the Concern's first letter back unsigned.

objectives.text: Get Dorcas running

contract.journal: Ida signed the Concern's exclusive and Whitlock fitted a new board. Dorcas runs, on the Concern's board and the Concern's terms: twenty years of its freight first on every path.

dark.journal: Dorcas's board was woken without the Concern's channel. She runs dark: nobody up the hill can switch her off again. The Concern's man left Yard Nine the next morning.

spare.journal: Dorcas runs on Halina Wrona's last spare, a pre-war board with nobody in it but the maker. If one of the instruments at Four Ways goes now, it stays gone.

routes.label: Talk the keeper down
Tighten and peen the bolts yourself at night
Tell the stationmaster who is loosening the track
Get the halts paid again, so she has no need

bolts.journal: Gerrit Haas, East Halt's old line-keeper, finds the bolts on two joints of the east length backed off every morning, a rail's width from coming apart under a train, and tightens them every morning.

objectives.text: Find out who is loosening them

plan.journal: East Halt's keeper, Imani Wekesa, is loosening the east length herself, to throw the Concern's through off the rails at her halt: a wreck the guild must stop to clear, and nineteen cars for a dying halt to strip. Willem Visser drives it.

objectives.text: Decide what happens on the east length

stopped.journal: Imani tightened every bolt she had loosened, in daylight, while Gerrit watched with his hat off.

stood_down.journal: When the trains began to stop at the halts again, Imani tightened the east length herself the same morning, and never said why.

fixed.journal: I tightened and peened every bolt on the east length in the dark. In the morning Gerrit stood at the joint a long time and looked at the keeper's house, and said nothing.

told.journal: I told the stationmaster. His watch put Imani Wekesa off the Line at dawn. East Halt has thirteen people.

helped.journal: I helped Imani loosen the east length. The through comes past East Halt at two.

objectives.text: The through, at two

derailed.journal: The Concern's through came off the rails on the east length at two in the morning. East Halt strips its cars in a line, and the guild will be stopping there for a season.

routes.label: Stand up at the Stilt Court with what the water knows
Down Hum's leg to the export valve: shut it, or sleeve it to run clean
Dive for Kai's net under the Gut, and down Hum's leg
The tide post's box at night: the factor's day-book
Hum's board, the pressure log and the night barge: put it together
Make the guild pay the price of a barge before the whole village
The guild's night barge at Blackcap

burial.journal: Gull Stilts: a fishing village on stilts over a drowned town, with a skin on the water like a bruise. The day I came, a boy of eleven went out on the ebb off the old steps: Kai Tanoa, who dove under the boardwalks for his mother's net and did not come up. His mother says the Rigs' oil killed him, and has called the Stilt Court.

objectives.text: Speak to Kai's mother
Find whoever keeps the court

claim.journal: Oona Brack keeps the Book of Water on a grounded ferry, the Greta, and the court sits on her car deck. Page nine: a life for a life, or a boat for a life. The court will hear Lua Tanoa's claim against the Rigs when somebody stands up with what the water knows: who fouled it, and that they knew. Everybody on the Stilts says the Rig. Saying is cheap.

objectives.text: Find where the oil comes from
See the Rigs for yourself
Find Kai's net under the Gut

hum.journal: Hum, the platform that still pumps, has an old export line to a drowned tank at Blackcap, and its board reads it open. Hamid Farouk, who keeps Hum, says the line was cut before he was born and the board lies; his daughter says the pressure has fallen eleven points since the thaw because something is drinking. The valve is down Hum's north-east leg, under the water.

objectives.text: Go down Hum's north-east leg to the export valve

seal.journal: Nobody on Hum opened the line. The guild did: its diver went down the leg at night and turned the export wheel, and sealed it TOLLMEN — LINE ACCOUNT, so Hum's oil runs under the Stilts to the guild's tank at Blackcap, and the guild's barge loads two tankers a month for the price of one. The old line leaks at every joint. The factor calls it shrinkage. The tide post is also the shore's only buyer of fish and seller of salt and medicine, and its anchorage is half the widows' bread.

objectives.text: Something the court can hold: the seal, the post's tally, the barge's manifest, the guild's diver
Decide what to do with Hum's export valve
Have Oona call the court on Lua's claim

ruled_guild.journal: The Stilt Court found the guild had opened Hum's line and that Kai Tanoa drowned in what it leaked. A boat for a life: the guild paid. Hum's crew keep Hum, and the guild buys one tanker from their deck. Whatever else the shore has lost by it, the Book says what happened.

ruled_sea.journal: The Stilt Court found the sea had taken Kai Tanoa. His mother walked off the Greta and out of Gull Stilts. The guild's barge loads at Blackcap at night, and the water under the Gut is black.

taking.journal: The Stilt Court found Hum's oil had killed Kai Tanoa and gave the Rig to Gull Stilts for his life. Page three: anything that floats and works is a boat. The Stilts' boats are going out to take Hum from forty people who have never lived anywhere else.

objectives.text: Be on Hum when the Stilts' boats come

ruled_rig.journal: Hamid Farouk took Hum's crew off the platform before the Stilts' boats came, and went up the delta for the Line. Hum is Gull Stilts' now. The turbine still hums. Somebody on the Stilts will have to learn how not to let her stop.

ruled_rig_blood.journal: Hamid Farouk would not give Hum up, and the Stilts took her off him. He is dead on his own deck. Hum is Gull Stilts' now, and the crew that is left works her for the village, and does not speak to anyone from it.

decision.text: Gull Stilts took Hum by force; Hamid Farouk died on his own deck.

news.text: Gull Stilts took the Rigs by force; the old keeper died on his deck

routes.label: Argue that the water gave him back
The guild's collections in the tide post's day-book
The Curlew's oars, the brand on his wrist, the patch on her bow
Make the finder say it
Buy him a skiff and send him up the delta

back.journal: A man walked into Gull Stilts on the Meridian road whom the Book of Water says drowned two years ago: Mateo Ibarra. His boat, the Curlew, was found adrift with his coat aboard and went to its finder by page twelve; the finder married his wife.

objectives.text: Talk to the man at the Landing

book.journal: Mateo wants his boat and his wife, if she wants him. The Book says what the water takes is the water's, and a boat found on the water is the finder's. Rui Sousa found the Curlew and married Paz; they have a baby. The court will hear Mateo if he stands up and asks.

objectives.text: Find out where Mateo has been for two years
Talk to Paz
Talk to Rui Sousa
Have Oona call the court for him

turn.journal: Mateo never went in the water. The guild's press took him off the Gut at night for three hundred Tolls owed at the tide post and sold him to its own barges, and set the Curlew adrift with his coat aboard so the shore would write him drowned. Rui Sousa told them where he slept. The Curlew was his fee. Paz does not know.

objectives.text: Settle it: at the court, or outside it

living.journal: The Stilt Court wrote a new page: what the water gives back is not the water's. The Curlew is Mateo's again, and Paz was asked, for once, and answered for herself.

sold.journal: The court heard that Rui Sousa sold his neighbour to the press for a boat, and put him off the stilts. Paz lives alone with the baby. Mateo moors the Curlew under her loft and waits.

written.journal: The court kept page twelve: Mateo Ibarra is still the water's. He went out to the Rigs, where they take anyone who can carry, and from Hum's flare stack you can see the Curlew if you know where to look.

quiet.journal: I paid for a skiff and Mateo Ibarra rowed up the delta again, and left Paz be. She will never know what Rui did, unless somebody tells her. Nobody on the Stilts is going to.

routes.label: Lean's cut gas line, the soot on the Jesty, the Book of wrecks
Read the wreck's heading and the parapet
Make the wrecker stop, and nobody need know
Bring it to the Stilt Court instead of the guild
Sell the guild a name

wreck.journal: A guild salt barge lies broken on the Jesty, a drowned hotel's roof, and two of her men drowned in the fog. The factor at the tide post offers a hundred for the wreckers who hung a lamp on the roof where no lamp should be, while Lean's light was dark. The Stilts' divers are stripping the wreck by salvage right: what the water wrecks, the water gives.

objectives.text: Find out why Lean's light was dark
Search the Jesty's parapet
Read the wrecks in the Book of Water

turn.journal: Yewande Coker, the dive master. Since the sheen killed the fish she has put out Lean's light in fog and hung her own on the Jesty, and the guild's barges steer for it like home; her divers strip them for the salt and twine and medicine the post sells at a usurer's price, and Gull Stilts has eaten this season on it. The two bargemen are the first dead. Her daughter rows the lamp out.

objectives.text: Decide who judges the false light

exposed.journal: I gave Yewande Coker to the guild for a hundred Tolls. She gave herself up at the tide post so that nobody would ask about her girl, and the guild hanged her from the post at dawn. Ade Bankole keeps the dive stage now.

court.journal: The Stilt Court judged the false light, not the guild. It took Yewande Coker's boat, and her salvage for the drowned men's kin, and did what it decided with the rest of her. The guild did not get its hanging.

stopped.journal: Yewande dropped the lamp off her stage into Ellery and watched it go down. Nobody but me knows she ever hung it. The guild's notice stays on the board until the salt crusts it over.

framed.journal: I gave the guild Ewan Tulloch, Lean's lamp-keeper, whose light was dark because somebody cut his line. They hanged him from the tide post at dawn. Yewande Coker does not look at me.

routes.label: On Coker's hose at slack water
Buy a diving bag and breathe your own air

first.journal: Yewande Coker takes divers down to Ellery, the drowned town under Gull Stilts, at slack water: six Tolls on her hose for the roofs, and you keep what you bring up. The city's tide table at the Landing says when the water is slack.

objectives.text: Dive Ellery's roofs

more.journal: Ellery gives what she has once, and then less. The high street is eight fathoms down, past the roofs; Hum's crew dive the legs of Stump, out at the Rigs, sixty feet and more, for the boards and controllers the platform's builders left in the dark.

objectives.text: Dive the high street
Dive Stump's legs at the Rigs

done.journal: I have dived all three: the roofs, the high street and Hum's legs. They still give, a little, at every slack.

routes.label: Lay what happened before the Harbour court on the Customs House steps
The box's weight, the crane's tape, the dead man's tin: put it together
Read the load tape in Crane Six's cab
The bond officer's drawer, at night
Bring the Stand to black the Bond
Sell what you found to whoever pays
Stand on the line against the guild's hired men

fallen.journal: At Carrick, Meridian's docks across the dry river, a box fell from Crane Six in the night onto the man under it: Dmytro Lysenko, the night gang's hooker-on. The guild's tally board says he unlatched the spreader wrong, and has stood his gang down without pay and his widow without a funeral tally. Constance Okoye, who speaks for the dockers at the Stand, says Dmytro never unlatched a box wrong in eleven years.

objectives.text: Talk to Constance Okoye at the Stand
Look at the box

digging.journal: The box is stencilled fourteen tonnes and weighed thirty. The Harbour Master, Factor Henrike Dahl, hears the quay's quarrels on the Customs House steps at the change of shift, and she will hear Gang Nine's appeal when somebody brings her what happened. Crane Six has a cutout that should refuse a load like that.

objectives.text: Find out why Crane Six lifted it
Talk to the widow
Talk to the night gang-master
Ask why nobody weighed it

override.journal: Somebody turned Crane Six's overload cutout off with the night key a minute before the spreader let go. The night key is the gang-master's, and Mattias Platt says it never left his belt. The guild bills the Concern's freight by the ton and has not weighed a box off the through in two years.

objectives.text: Find out who turned the key

turn.journal: Dmytro turned it himself, with a key he had cut, on the Bond's night pass. The Concern's bond officer pays a hand on the night gang to lift its boxes past Crane Six's cutout, because its boxes are billed at half their weight and a box the cutout refuses would have to be weighed; Dmytro took his pay in the blue inhalers his daughter breathes through. The guild's verdict is true, and a lie. The dockers' grievance is just, and wrong. And the man who paid sits in the Bond, where by the Harbour Act the Harbour Master's word stops at the fence.

objectives.text: Decide what the quay is told, and by whom

stoppage.journal: The Stand has blacked the Bond: no docker on the quay will touch a Concern box until the Concern pays for Dmytro and its boxes go over the weighbridge. Sealed boxes stack up under the Bond's white lights and the through waits at the yard throat. The guild has sent to the Ring for men who will work a crane for a day's pay, and they will be on the Stand at dawn.

objectives.text: Be on the Stand at dawn when the hired men come

bond.journal: I put the whole of it before the Harbour court: the box's weight, the tape, the tin. Factor Dahl found that Dmytro Lysenko turned the cutout at the Bond's pay, and that the guild's weighbridge had been blind to the through for two years by its own order. Every Concern box goes over the plate now. Gang Nine stands on the line again. Dmytro's name is the name of the man who sold the cutout.

gang.journal: I argued Gang Nine's appeal on the short gang, and kept the tin out of it. Factor Dahl found that a gang worked five where the crane needs eight is the master's fault and not the hand's, and paid the funeral tally out of the guild's own box. The quay thinks the guild killed Dmytro. The Bond's boxes still go unweighed, and somebody else on the night gang has a key now.

guild.journal: I gave Factor Dahl the tin in her office with the door shut. She thanked me, paid a finder's fee, and sent the Concern a bill for two years of back-freight in a sealed envelope. The tally board still says DOCKER'S NEGLIGENCE. Gang Nine is still stood down. The guild has what it wanted, which was to know.

bought.journal: Lucien Roux paid me for what I had found, and nobody else will see it. The tally board says what it said. Gang Nine is off the line, and Oksana Lysenko has moved her girl down to the Hulls. Somewhere on the night gang there is a new key.

black_won.journal: The Ring's men went home. The Concern paid Oksana Lysenko the price of a funeral and a season, through the guild, without a word; its boxes go over the weighbridge now, and Gang Nine stands on the line. The Stand found out what it is when it stands together. So did the guild, and the Bond.

black_broken.journal: The stoppage broke on the Stand at dawn. The Ring's men worked Crane Six for a day's pay and the Bond's boxes moved. Gang Nine is off the line for good, and Constance Okoye does not stand on it any more; she drives Crane Two and says nothing to anybody.

routes.label: Down the delta on the tide boat, where nobody reads the Concern's paper
The Line to West Halt and the track south to the Choir by night
Buy her paper from the bond officer
Ask the Harbour court whether a person can be under bond
Take the Bond's sixty

notice.journal: A notice on the guild floor's door at Carrick, in the Concern's clean type: RETURNABLE LOST FROM BOND — ONE — REWARD 60. The dockers say something came off the through in an empty box last week, and that it was not a thing.

objectives.text: Find out what the Bond has lost

found.journal: Mirela Stan, fifteen, from the Skirts, rode six days west in the dark in a box of spares, and Espe hides her at the back of the cookshop. The Bond calls her a returnable. Its officer will pay sixty for her, and put her on the through east.

objectives.text: Find out what a returnable is

paper.journal: She is the surety on her mother's Concern contract: returnable on default or flight. Her flight is the default. Her mother wrote GO on the back of the paper. Wherever Mirela goes, the Concern's paper says what it says.

objectives.text: Decide with her where she goes

returned.journal: I took the Bond's sixty. Mirela Stan went back east on the through, returnable, in the kind of box she came in.

shore.journal: Mirela went down the delta on the tide boat to Gull Stilts, where the water keeps no paper. The Concern's paper went with her, folded small in her coat.

choir.journal: Mirela rode the seven o'clock east to West Halt and walked south by the track at night to Openfield, where the Choir takes anyone the sky can see. Her paper says what it says. Nobody at Openfield can read it.

bought.journal: I bought Mirela's paper off the Bond. The surety is paid, her mother's contract is whole, and the paper is hers to burn. She burned it in Espe's stove and stayed to wash pots, for wages.

ruled.journal: The Harbour court found that a person is not goods under the Harbour Act, and cannot be under bond. In Carrick Mirela Stan is a passenger who owes her fare, which I paid. On the quay, the Concern's paper is waste. In the Skirts it is still a contract.

routes.label: The Harbour Act and the crew books before the Harbour court
Find the old tram bridge's footing and re-site the abutment
Make House Vane pay a real price for all nine hulls together
Carry House Vane's purse to the masters who have not signed

stakes.journal: On the dry bed under Carrick's river wall, nine pre-war ships sit where the river left them ninety years ago, and three hundred people live in them: the Hulls. House Vane's surveyor has driven blue stakes among them for the far end of the Crown's new bridge, and the Harbour Master has leased the berths to the house for works.

objectives.text: Talk to whoever speaks for the Hulls
Talk to House Vane's surveyor
Read the Harbour's notice

masters.journal: The bridge's far end has to land on the Hulls' bed because the old bridge's pier footing is there, and the Crown wants its road to the Docks so its freight comes up into the city without going round by the Wall, or past the gate's lens. The Hulls' living is the cradle, a basket on a wire over the bed to Bridgeward at night. House Vane is not evicting anyone: it is buying the hulls' masters' marks on papers of abandonment, forty Tolls a hull, and three have signed.

objectives.text: Decide what happens to the Hulls

cleared.journal: The masters signed and the Hulls were abandoned on paper, and then in fact: the Harbour Master's men cleared the berths at dawn and three hundred people carried their bedding up the river stairs into the Boxes. The cradle's cable is cut. House Vane's far end has its ground.

crewed.journal: The Harbour court read Schedule 3 and the crew books, and found that a crewed vessel in port cannot be moved by a lease. The Hulls stay. The cradle runs at night. House Vane's stakes are still in the bed, waiting for a master who will sign.

sold.journal: The nine masters sold the Hulls to House Vane together, at three times the house's price, and walked up the river stairs with the money in a bag between two of them. The cradle went with the berths. Some of the Hulls bought boxes on the quay; some went over into the city the way they used to send everyone else.

moved.journal: Imogen Thrale moved the far end downstream to the old tram bridge's footing, under the edge of the Concern's Bond. The Hulls stay. House Vane and the Concern now want the same hundred metres of quay.

routes.label: Read the Concern's requests card to Number Four at the lamp meeting
Make the winchwoman end the arrangement herself
Take the winchwoman's tin money for silence
Fight the Clean at the switchback below the col
Bring the family down the old drift under the mountain

taken.journal: Number Four, the free pit on the Teeth's south face, chalks the names of the runaways the Clean take on the path below the col under a line on its lamp board: three this year. The Shift's runner there, Desmond Achebe, is waiting for a woman and her son to come over the col.

objectives.text: Bring the family down from the col
Find out how the Clean know who is coming over

arrangement.journal: Number Four is free by arrangement. Ragna Holm, who walked its first dozen over the col, tells the Clean on her set when somebody the Concern wants comes over, a name a season, and the Concern pays double for Four's tin through the guild and lets the pit stand.

objectives.text: Find out what the letters on the Concern's card mean
Decide what becomes of the arrangement

exposed.journal: I read the Concern's card to Number Four at the lamp meeting. Four voted Ragna Holm down the mountain and broke her set. Its tin sells at the ordinary price now, and the Concern's eye is on it.

ended.journal: Ragna Holm ended her arrangement herself, on the set and at the board, and stepped down, and winds the cage still. Number Four is poorer, and its own.

kept.journal: I took Ragna Holm's tin money and kept her secret. Number Four stays free and fed, and the Concern takes a name a season off its path.

fought.journal: I fought the Clean on the col. The Concern ended its arrangement with Number Four itself by stopping the money. Four is poorer, and watched.

routes.label: Pull the machine's controller
Wake it to dig for Number Four, through Kes or a grid link
Stop the pumps and let the water back over it

below.journal: Gaspard Okoro's pumps have Number Four's lower level half dry for the first time in seventy years, and the face crew came up white: something down there moved.

objectives.text: Go down to the old level and see what moved

digger.journal: In the old level under Number Four a pre-war mining machine of the Concern's lineage lies where it was stopped, its lamp blinking, waiting to be told to work again.

objectives.text: Decide what to do with the digger

salvaged.journal: I pulled the digger's controller. It is a dead machine now, and the lower level is Four's to dig by hand.

tamed.journal: The digger cuts for Number Four now. It is the Concern's machine, and answers to the Concern's words.

drowned.journal: I let the water back over the digger. The lower level is lost again.

routes.label: Put the truth about the dam into the city's record, with its keeper
Make the gauge read full without the block, before the inspection
Show the inspector the block, for the record's bounty
Fight the inspection on the crest

audit.journal: The city says Ashby Dam has delivered short of its schedule for eleven seasons, and has sent an assessor up the river to read the gauge. The barges at Low Landing go down half-loaded on a low river. The assessor waits at the dam for the keeper.

objectives.text: Find out why Ashby is short
Find out why the keepers do it
Find out what the shortfall costs

lie.journal: Ashby has never been full. Its keepers wedge the gauge so the city's controller reads a lake that is not there, and the city plans its water on it.

objectives.text: Find out why the keepers do it
Find out what the shortfall costs
Decide what the inspection finds

truth.journal: The truth about Ashby is in the city's record. The city will plan its water on the real lake: the Precinct's growth cut, the Sink's spring pumps its own again, the river let down even.

hidden.journal: The city's inspector found Ashby compliant. The keepers' lie holds, and so does everything it costs.

exposed.journal: The city took Ashby's keepers down the river, and wardens keep the dam to the city's card. The Water is to be raised to its full line.

sunk.journal: I fought the city's inspection on Ashby's crest. The record has written its assessor lost in the Wet.

routes.label: Say it all at the crews' meeting in the mill
Tell the Ridge's foreman alone what happened to his son
Give the boom-keeper the mark-cutter, for the boom's money
Keep watch while the Ridge burns the Bottoms' camp

marks.journal: At Sawtown's boom somebody cuts the Ridge crew's mark off their logs at night and cuts the Bottoms' hook over it, and the boom pays the Bottoms. The two crews have been feuding for two years, since the Ridge foreman's son died under a falling tree. The boom-keeper wants the cutter found before the Ridge finds them.

objectives.text: Find the mark-cutter
Find out where the money goes
Find out how Mikkel Brandvold died

cutter.journal: The mark-cutter is Sigrun Brandvold, the Ridge foreman's own daughter, and the money goes to the woman his dead son meant to marry and the son's baby, whom the Ridge will not own.

objectives.text: Find out how Mikkel Brandvold died
Decide what happens at Sawtown

truth.journal: At the crews' meeting in the mill, Mikkel Brandvold's death was said aloud for what it was. His father gave up the Ridge and went up the hill. The feud is over; the marks stopped.

quiet.journal: I told Arvid Brandvold alone. He went to the cookhouse and held his son's child. The feud is over, and nobody else knows why.

caught.journal: I gave the boom-keeper Sigrun Brandvold's name and not her reason. Sawtown puts mark-cutters on the Water. The feud goes on.

burned.journal: I kept watch for Cillian Moss. The Bottoms' camp burned, and the Bottoms went down the river.

routes.label: See the load to the guild's man in the city and take the pay
Put the load over the side in the deep reach
Take the load and its waybill to the wardens at the city gate

load.journal: Magda Kowal's barge, the Patience, has been tied up at Low Landing half a season with her mooring owed to the guild. The guild's factor has a sealed load for the city at a hundred and fifty, and she needs a hand at the sweeps and somebody awake on the night reach.

objectives.text: Crew the Patience down the river
Find out what the cases hold
See the load to its end

delivered.journal: The guild has its twelve cases at the city's Docks: the Concern's kennel boards. Magda Kowal has her mooring.

river.journal: Twelve cases of the Concern's kennel boards are in the mud of the deep reach above the city. Magda Kowal owes the guild her mooring.

wardens.journal: The wardens at the city gate have the guild's twelve cases of kennel boards, and its waybill. The guild knows my face.
